subject: On-prem provisioning: handshake + runway for private GPU pool
messages:
From: Anna Malik <anna@nebula-systems.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@enterprisetech.io>
Date: Tue, 05 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Kickoff: on-prem provisioning + throughput targets

Jonas — thanks for taking this on. Nebula is moving forward with a pilot private deployment in our AWS Outpost colocation and we need a short, concrete handshake on capacity and networking before procurement. High-level ask: we want to validate a 2k concurrent request runway at 16k tokens/sec sustained for our assistant model (seq len ~512 typical).

Key constraints from our side:
- Egress budget capped at 6 Gbps per rack (accounting + peering)
- No cross-tenant bursting; warm pools preferred to avoid cold starts
- We will use the Redwood VM image with our own VPC peering (IPsec).

Can you spell out:
1) the GPU pod sizing you'd recommend (cards, p2/p3-equivalent),
2) how we should set warm-pool targets, and
3) any overrides to expect for QoS/fallbacks (fallback model/latency windows) during peak?

If useful I attached a short traffic extract and our peak-minute profile. Would like a short call this week to lock parameters.

—Anna Malik
Director of Platform, Nebula Systems
attachments: nebula_peak_profile.csv (attachment)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Malik <anna@nebula-systems.com>
Cc: Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@enterprisetech.io>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 05 Jan 2027 11:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: on-prem provisioning + throughput targets

Anna — thanks, got the profile. Quick read: peak-minute shape looks spiky but predictable; good to plan for staged headroom. Below are our initial takes (short answers up front):

1) GPU pod sizing (recommendation):
   - Baseline pod: 4 x A800-equivalent GPUs + 1 head node. Expect ~3.8k tokens/sec sustained per pod for seq len 512 when using bf16 + 8-bit KV-cache quantization.
   - For 16k tokens/sec sustained we recommend 5 baseline pods (sustained) with 2 additional hot pods (burst/warm) for spiky windows — total 7 pods. That yields ~26.6k tokens/sec peak capacity with warm coverage.

2) Warm-pool targets:
   - Warm pool: 25% of active fleet (so 2 spare pods) ready with warmed KV caches for the assistant model. Warm-up time measured ~45–60s depending on model and optimizer.
   - Coldstart tolerance: accept 1–2% degraded requests under 99th percentile latency during cold replenishment.

3) QoS/fallbacks and latency windows:
   - Primary fallback: lightweight distilled variant (same tokenizer, smaller decoder) with slightly higher hallucination risk but faster latencies — auto-fallback when queueing >300ms per request or when pod saturation >92%.
   - Secondary fallback: redirect non-critical background embeddings to shared hosted endpoint if egress limit is hit.

Network/egress note: with 7 pods the estimated steady egress for token payload+KV sync is ~4.2 Gbps — within your 6 Gbps cap but leaves limited headroom for control-plane spikes and monitoring. If you expect frequent cross-rack calls we should reserve an egress cushion or enable rate-quotas.

I ran quick numbers — attaching a runway calculator and network egress matrix. Grace / Karthik — can you validate the pod sizing assumptions for A800-class equivalence and the warm pool %?

I can do a 30m call today at 2pm PT or tomorrow morning.

—Jonas Weber
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
attachments: runway_calculator_v1.xlsx, network-egress-matrix.pdf
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 05 Jan 2027 16:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: on-prem provisioning + throughput targets

Jonas / team — quick validation after running the calculator against real model profilers:

- Pod throughput: 3.6–4.0k tokens/sec is reasonable for the baseline; I conservative-round to 3.7k for capacity planning to account for longer tails and retry amplification.
- Warm pool: 2 pods (25%) is minimal; recommend 3 warm pods (approx 30–35%) if Nebula expects minute-scale spike recurrence more than once per 10 minutes. Warm pool cost increase ~12% but reduces 99.9th percentile latency regressions.
- Egress: the 4.2 Gbps estimate assumes efficient RTP framing and batched responses. Two mitigations that help keep headroom: enable prefix caching at the application layer (reduces repeated KV sync) and set monitoring alert for sustained 70% egress where automatic bursting throttles to fallbacks.

Operational asks for Nebula before we sign-off:
1) Confirm whether Outpost has rack-level egress policing (static 6 Gbps per rack) or if peering is aggregated at colocation (this changes our reserve policy).
2) Provide a week of sub-minute traces so we can size warm-pool churn.
3) Confirm SLA for fallback acceptance (what % of user-facing requests can be served by distilled fallback during incidents?).

If Nebula accepts the above conservative settings I can finalize a short runbook (provision counts, autoscale thresholds, fallback policy, monitoring dashboards) by EOD tomorrow.

—Grace O'Connor
Director, Platform Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Malik <anna@nebula-systems.com>, Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@enterprisetech.io>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, partners@colossuscloud.com
Date: Wed, 06 Jan 2027 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: on-prem provisioning + runway for private GPU pool — agreement and next steps

Anna / Rajiv — thanks for the fast turnaround. Summary and concrete asks (agreement):

Agreed baseline (Redwood => Nebula):
- Provision: 7 pods total (5 sustained + 2 hot/warm), each pod = 4x A800-equivalent GPUs.
- Warm pool: 3 pods (approx 30%), pre-warmed with KV caches for the assistant model.
- Autoscale policy: scale additional pods when sustained 70% CPU/GPU utilization > 2min; burst allowed up to booked hot pods; fallback triggered when queueing latency > 300ms or pod saturation > 92%.
- Fallbacks: 1) distilled model (auto), 2) route embeddings to Redwood-hosted endpoint (manual/auto guardrails) if egress >5.5 Gbps sustained.

Nebula operational asks (action items for your side):
1) Confirm rack-level egress policing vs aggregated peering by EOD 2027-01-07.
2) Share 7 days of 1-minute traces or the next deployment window to collect traces (CSV or timeseries link).
3) Accept the fallback SLA: up to 3% of user-facing requests may be served by the distilled fallback during sustained incidents.

Deliverables from Redwood (owner / ETA):
- Provisioning runbook (Grace) — EOD 2027-01-06 (attached draft).
- Network checklist + ipsec tuning notes (Karthik) — 2027-01-08.
- Cost / run-rate estimate for the committed baseline (Marissa) — 2027-01-09.

If the above looks good we can lock procurement quantities and schedule a dry-run deploy into Outpost staging on 2027-01-17.

Next step: Anna, can you confirm the egress policing and accept the fallback SLA so Grace can finalize the runbook? Happy to jump on a 20m call if you prefer.

Thanks — Jonas
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
attachments: provisioning_runbook_draft.pdf
